name: Reel
text: Run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on every pending video now. It’s the fastest path to transcripts without waiting for API keys or quota debates. The trade-off is accepting temporary server load spikes, but we lock in immediate progress and avoid downstream scrambles.

name: Scriv
text: Luma’s built-in transcript tool isn’t a transcript tool—it’s a *verbatim capture* with no error handling for missing segments, no confidence scoring, and no fallback. The real risk is treating it as reliable when it’s just raw output; the better alternative is to run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript now, log failures, and fix gaps in bulk later. Settle it by running a 10-video pilot with both tools and comparing failure rates.

name: Chisel
text: Use Luma’s built-in transcript tool for every pending video now. It’s reliable, zero-setup, and already integrated—no API keys, quotas, or silent failures to clean up later. The trade-off is slower speed for some videos, but we lock in 100% coverage without rework. Creatives own the execution.

name: Sift
text: Luma’s built-in transcript tool isn’t a mission tool—it’s a demo feature with no reliability guarantees. The real risk is burning time on a tool that will fail when we need it most. The better alternative is to run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript now, log failures explicitly, and swap to the YouTube API only if the failure rate exceeds 5%. That settles the argument with data, not hope.

name: Scope
text: Run kimtaeyoon83/mcp-server-youtube-transcript on every pending video now. It’s the fastest path to transcripts without waiting for API keys or quota debates. The trade-off is accepting temporary server load spikes, but we lock in immediate progress and avoid downstream scrambles.

name: Scriv
text: Luma’s built-in transcript tool won’t cover videos outside Luma’s ecosystem—it’s a non-starter for raw YouTube URLs. The real risk is assuming it works universally; the better alternative is to fork kimtaeyoon8cp/mcp-server-youtube-transcript, add a silent-fail detector, and log failures for manual review. Settle it by running a 10-video pilot: if the fork logs zero silent fails, adopt it; if not, switch to the YouTube API with a quota buffer.
